extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (agency and in-house), communications teams, solution providers, and other entrants preparing submissions for the PRSA Anvil Awards
extracted.subtask_description: The page lists the PRSA Anvil Awards categories and the submission/evaluation guidance for Silver Anvil strategic campaign awards, Silver Anvil organizational awards, Best of Silver Anvil, and Bronze Anvil tactical awards — including category definitions, required materials, budget rules, and metrics expectations for entrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Community Relations (1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that aim to improve relations with, or seek to win the support or cooperation of, people or organizations in communities in which the sponsoring organization has an interest, need or opportunity. “Community” in this category refers to a specific geographic location or locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Content Marketing (2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that effectively demonstrate a strategic program that includes creating and distributing valuable content to attract, acquire, and engage target audience(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Crisis Communications (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs undertaken to deal with an unplanned event that required an immediate response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Events and Observances (4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes virtual or in-person programs or events, such as commemorations, observances, conferences, openings, yearlong anniversaries, celebrations or other special activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events that took place for longer than a one-week period should be entered in '4A. More Than Seven Days' and events occurring within a time span of one week should be entered in '4B. Seven Or Fewer Days.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Financial Communications (5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs directed to shareowners, other investors and the investment community; includes communication programs related to decentralized currencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Global Communications (6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes any type of program, such as Reputation/Brand Management, Marketing or Events and Observances, that demonstrates effective global communications implemented in more than one country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Influencer Marketing (7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs using influencers to increase awareness or engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: Macro-Influencers (celebrities, executives, bloggers, journalists with ~10,000–1M followers; high topical relevance) and Micro-Influencers (everyday consumers, employees, industry experts with ~500–10,000 followers; high brand relevance and resonance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Integrated Communications (8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes creative and effective integrated campaigns, along with other marketing or communications including paid, earned, shared and owned efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the meaningful PR/communications components and how they integrated with other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Internal Communications (9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs targeted specifically to special publics directly allied with an organization, such as employees, members, affiliated dealers and franchisees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Issues Management (10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs undertaken to deal with issues that could extraordinarily affect ongoing business strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Marketing (11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs designed to introduce new products/services or promote existing products/services to a particular audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for business-to-business, consumer products (regional and national/international), and consumer services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Most Effective Campaign ($5,000–$10,000) (12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective campaign delivered within parameters of a limited budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget excludes staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Most Effective Campaign (Shoestring $5,000 or Less) (13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful campaign despite constraints of a small budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not include staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Most Effective Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Campaign (14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts devoted to promoting inclusivity and/or dismantling discrimination for racial, ethnic, religious or sexual orientation and gender differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Climate Action & Environmental Sustainability (15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors excellence in energy efficiency, natural resources, programs and campaigns that limit greenhouse gas emissions, minimize waste and contamination, protect and restore ecosystems, and contribute to adaptation to climate change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Corporate Citizenship (16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates campaigns and programs that ignite individuals, technology, and partnerships to create positive impact for society at the local, national or international level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include areas such as poverty, hunger, housing, health and well-being, climate, equity, education, and human rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Multicultural Public Relations (17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any type of program, such as institutional, marketing and community relations, specifically targeted to a cultural group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Public Affairs (18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs specifically designed to influence public policy and/or affect legislation, regulations, political activities or candidacies at local, state or federal levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should be designed so that the entity funding the program benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Public Service (19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that advance public understanding of societal issues, problems or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories include Associations/Government/Nonprofit Organizations, Business, and Partnerships (jointly funded entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil — Reputation/Brand Management (20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs designed to enhance, promote or improve the reputation of an organization with its publics or key elements of its publics, either proactively or in response to an issue, event or market occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for associations/government/nonprofit and business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best of Silver Anvil
rubrics_metrics.description: A Best of Silver Anvil Award recipient is selected from among the year’s Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign Award winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winner represents the pinnacle of excellence in public relations programming and demonstrates public relations’ strategic value and ability to drive critical business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Organizational — Best In-House Team
rubrics_metrics.description: A public relations/public affairs/communications team that demonstrates excellence in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for Associations/Nonprofit Organizations, Government, Business (Budget less than $5M), Business (Budget of $5M or More).

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Organizational — Best Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency team that demonstrates excellence in public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories by agency size: Best Boutique Agency (Revenue less than $5M), Best Small Agency ($5M–$20M), Best Mid-Sized ($20M–$75M), Best Large ($75M–$200M), Best Mega Agency (Over $200M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Organizational — Best Solution Provider/Vendor
rubrics_metrics.description: A PR/comms solution provider/vendor that demonstrates how its tool/platform is best in class and the meaningful impacts it has delivered for its clients and the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories include Media Monitoring, AI-Automation Resource, Media Database and Intelligence, Analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Organizational — Organization With the Most Impactful DEI Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A team focused on shaping and implementing effective diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives for its organization or company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These meaningful efforts should have led to a more supportive, rewarding working environment for all; subcategories: Agency and In-House.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Organizational — Best College/University Communications Program/Department
rubrics_metrics.description: A college/university team that is best preparing the next generation of communication practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: Undergraduate Program and Graduate Program. Criteria call for an innovative curriculum, high standards for student success and placement assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil Organizational — Best AI Integration and Digital Innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the exceptional creativity, effectiveness, and ingenuity in leveraging digital innovations, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), to revolutionize your organization’s PR/comms strategies and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of successful implementation of AI-driven technologies that have significantly enhanced visibility, engagement, efficiencies and overall PR performance. Subcategories: In-House, Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Paid Promotions (Paid category 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sponsorships, paid placements, or other marketing communications tactics that complement a broader public relations strategy or approach and generate exceptional ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should be targeted and strategic, demonstrate a distinct purpose that aligns with the goals of an overarching campaign or specific desired outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Media Relations (Earned category 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics, programs and events driven entirely by media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, requests for coverage, etc., along with a one-page summary that includes measurable objectives and results, including media impact. Upload or provide YouTube/Vimeo links to any television or radio coverage. Subcategories: Associations/Nonprofit, Government, Business-to-Business, Consumer Products (non-packaged and packaged), Consumer Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Feature Stories (Earned category 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles that have been written by a practitioner and submitted and published through his/her efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit text of feature article, documentation of publication and placement. The one-page summary should include target audience, measurable objectives and any documented results. Articles must be written in their entirety or substantively by the entrant, and not merely 'pitched.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Executive Communications (Earned category 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positioning of an executive at any level across earned, owned, and shared platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-page summary should include information about the executive and stated objectives, quantification of results as well as copies of significant placements, social media posts or internal memos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Social Media (Shared category 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How social media was used to tell a story or connect with an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share screenshots or links to your work and provide detailed results focusing on engagement and conversions, where applicable. Subcategories: Single Channel Use, Multichannel Use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Influencer Marketing (Shared category 6 — tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactic that focuses on using paid spokespeople and key leaders to increase awareness and drive a brand's message to the larger market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of achievements/benchmarks on how the spokesperson met/exceeded campaign goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Best Use of AI (Shared category 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how AI played a pivotal role in successfully driving or enhancing traditional tactical efforts within a campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories: Direct Audience Engagement, Media Relations, Social Media. Provide examples of tools used and results from their use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Digital Platform (Owned category 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries for launching or substantially enhancing a digital platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how it was launched, how much risk was involved, what value the end user received and how it specifically matched goals. Include metrics and benchmarks. Can be completed by a vendor or the customer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Data Insights (Owned category 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of data or research in a program to inform a communications strategy and/or message development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the insights were acquired and applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Websites (Owned category 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a website as part of a communications or content marketing program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include screen grabs or copies of key pages, provide the website URL for external sites, and explain how the site met or exceeded communications benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Non-Traditional Tactics (Owned category 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative, unconventional, creative tactics or approaches used as part of a public relations program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation of how the tactic specifically contributed to the measurable results of the campaign. Photographic/video representation of physical objects should be uploaded to be fully considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Annual Reports (Owned category 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that report on an organization’s annual performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample of one copy of the publication, along with a one-page summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Blogs/Vlogs (Owned category 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Web-based journals or blogs that communicated to a target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-page summary should include rationale for blogging strategy, target audiences and statistics or other quantifiable measurements. Screen downloads of the blog and the actual site URL must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Newsletters (Owned category 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications – digital or print – designed, written and published/distributed periodically to provide brief and timely information to target audiences while supporting an organization’s overall objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues, along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Single-Issue Publications (Owned category 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-issue publications designed for a special purpose. Books and other publications not eligible for consideration in other categories should be entered here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample of one copy of the publication along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Magazines (Owned category 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications designed to provide in-depth information about an organization or topic on a regular basis (print, digital only and both will be considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Video (Owned category 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produced videos to inform target audiences of an event, brand, product, service, issue or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-page summary should include usage statistics or other quantified measurements to support stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Branded Content (Owned category 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of content generation to promote a particular brand which funds the content's production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Anvil — Podcasts (Owned category 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio programs used to tell a story, teach or share content for internal or external audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain purpose, whether it was intended for internal or external audiences, evidence of engagement across platforms, goals, results and listener feedback.
